=== b0985c4d ===
docs: chunk-index dedup — ADR-0021, narrowed append-only claims, LEDGER row
Documents what shipped, including the parts that went wrong.

ADR-0021 records the design (dedup by content hash + chunking class,
canonical precedence, the record-subset eviction gate, Rule B for
drifted vault copies, and update notifying rather than acting) and,
deliberately, that the original premise was falsified mid-cycle rather
than sound from the start: byte-identical sources are not
interchangeable, because a per-source index file accumulates records
from every past version of that path.

It also records the forensic outcome of the defective gate running once
against a real index: 1,960 index files removed, of which exactly 2 had
no surviving byte-identical twin, both recoverable from git. An earlier
'25 records lost' estimate is withdrawn as unreproducible, and an
earlier '0 unsafe removals' claim in cb6b9540 is superseded by name,
since that audit predates the stronger gate. Fine-grained loss inside
the regenerable set remains unquantifiable and is stated as such.

Six doc surfaces asserted the chunk index is append-only and never
deletes. Each is narrowed rather than reversed: within a source nothing
changed, across sources a duplicate's index may be removed only when its
records are provably a subset of a retained twin's. That includes the
deployed learn skill, which agents read.

A new LEDGER row carries the measurements with their methods, and marks
two figures honestly as one-time operational observations that were
never re-measured after the fix -- including the duplicate-share metric
that motivated the cycle.

=== fb2c9f45 ===
fix(dedup): gate eviction on record subset; update notifies, never deletes
Two corrections to the dedup shipped earlier in this cycle, one of them
a data-loss defect that reached a real index before it was found.

The premise was false. Dedup gated deletion on source-byte identity, on
the reasoning that byte-identical sources are interchangeable. They are
not: mergeChunkRecords is append-only WITHIN a source, so each per-source
.jsonl accumulates records from every past version of that path. Two
sources identical today can hold disjoint historical records, and
deleting either loses what the other never had. Measured on the real
corpus: 124 of 6,612 surviving index files carry records from more than
one ingest day.

Eviction now requires, immediately before removing a duplicate: the
canonical's index file exists, and every one of the duplicate's record
content-hashes is already present in the canonical's. Anything else is
refused and reported. Content hash is the right equivalence here -- it
is sha256 of the record text, and the fields that differ between twins
are the ones mergeChunkRecords already treats as immaterial when it
keeps the older record on a hash match. The gate applies to both the
retroactive prune and the ingest-time eviction, which previously had no
canonical check at all.

Reconciling a group now processes the canonical before its duplicates,
so a same-run eviction compares against an index that has been written
rather than one that has not. The canonical's records are loaded once
per group instead of once per duplicate: a refused group keeps
DuplicateOf empty and re-runs the gate on every future ingest, including
every automatic learn sweep, so the re-read was unbounded.

engram update no longer runs the cleanup. It detects whether a duplicate
group exists -- one manifest read and an in-memory grouping, never
opening an index file -- and prints a notice pointing at
engram prune --duplicates, matching the notify-only convention already
used for the empty-file backlog. The sentinel mechanism is deleted
entirely: detection is stateless, so it re-notifies while duplicates
remain and goes quiet when they do not, where a sentinel would claim
done regardless. A destructive migration should run when the user asks
for it, not as a side effect of refreshing a binary.

=== 33481996 ===
fix(ingest): exclude .claude/jobs from the --auto sweep
The .claude ancestor sweep excluded projects, plugins, cache, todos and
nine others, but not jobs -- so ~3GB of agent harness scratch, including
whole snapshot copies of the vault, was swept and indexed on every run.
The .pi sweep already excluded it, and its own comment noted Claude has
the same subdir shape, so this was an oversight rather than a decision.

Forensics on a real incident attributed 1,397 of 1,960 removed duplicate
index files (71%) to that one tree. Excluding it stops the duplication
at the source instead of indexing content and deleting it later.

Deliberate access is unaffected: manual --sweep roots are built from
ExcludeDirs, not ClaudeExcludeDirs, so sweeping a specific job output
still works.

=== cb6b9540 ===
feat(prune): add --duplicates to clear already-indexed copies
Unit 3 stops new duplicates entering the index but leaves every existing
one in place, so the crowding it was built to fix persists until the
index is cleaned once.

prune --duplicates groups manifest entries by content hash and chunking
class, keeps selectCanonical's winner in each group, and removes the
rest. Deletion is gated on the retained twin's index file existing at
the moment of removal, so a group whose canonical was never indexed is
refused rather than collapsed. Removal failures are reported per item
and exit non-zero; the run is convergent, and --dry-run reports without
writing.

Refusals are classified: the structural case -- a group where no member
was ever indexed, because a zero-chunk source yields no index file --
collapses into one summary line, while a refusal whose sibling IS
indexed is printed individually, since only those indicate a real
anomaly. On the live corpus that is 47,394 structural and 0 anomalous.

Measured on a copy of the real index: 8,572 index files to 6,612
(-1,960, -23%), manifest 62,506 entries to 60,546, converging on the
second run. An audit written independently of this code confirmed all
1,960 removed entries still have their content represented by a
surviving entry whose index file exists -- 0 unsafe removals.

=== 85413e9e ===
fix(ingest): never dedup across chunking classes
Unit 3 grouped sources by content hash alone, on the premise that
byte-identical content is interchangeable. It isn't: chunkSource
dispatches on extension, so a .jsonl goes through the transcript
stripper and anything else through the markdown chunker. The same bytes
therefore yield different records -- markdown keeps the literal JSON,
the transcript path yields the stripped 'USER: ...' text -- and
discarding either twin would permanently lose its distinct chunking.

Grouping is now keyed on hash plus chunking class in both the ingest
dedup path and the prune path, so a .md and a .jsonl with identical
bytes are never duplicates of each other.

No live hash group currently spans extensions (0 of 6,874), so this
changes nothing about today's index -- it closes the gap before
something lands in it. Verified by injecting a synthetic same-hash
.md/.jsonl pair into a copy of the real index: both survive a full
dry-run, delete and re-run cycle untouched, with every other count
unchanged.

=== 364e60bc ===
feat(ingest): dedup byte-identical sources across the chunk index
79% of manifest sources were byte-identical copies of another source --
worktrees, backup-restore trees, /tmp config pools, job-dir vault
snapshots -- each indexed separately and competing for the same result
slots at query time.

Sources are now grouped by content hash before indexing, and only
selectCanonical's winner in each group is indexed; the rest are recorded
as manifestEntry.DuplicateOf pointing at it. Precedence is explicit
flags > repo root > closest .claude/.pi ancestor > other, tie-broken by
fewest path separators then lexicographically, so the winner does not
depend on walk order. A higher-precedence source arriving later evicts
the already-indexed lower-precedence twin.

Three supporting changes:
- sourceRef and SweepRoot carry origin + physical ancestor depth, which
  gatherSources previously discarded, so precedence has something real
  to rank by.
- The hash registry is seeded from the manifest's cached FileHash, so
  unchanged sources are never re-read -- pinned by a ReadFile call
  counter, since defeating it would otherwise pass every test.
- ingestSource's cheap-skip now also requires the index file to exist.
  It previously compared only the source's mtime+size, so a source whose
  index file went missing stayed silently unsearchable until something
  unrelated touched it.

Rule B: a swept .md with a sibling .vec.json is a vault-note copy and is
indexed only from the resolved vault path, catching drifted snapshots
that hash differently from the live note.

=== 5ec0ab2f ===
docs(plans): record Gate B findings — origin prerequisite, ExtraRoots exemption

=== 3307093a ===
fix(ingest): drop --auto sweep roots that sit under a throwaway path
NonPersistentPrefixes was attached only to the session-logs root, and it
matches slugified directory NAMES against entries during the walk. But
sweepListerFrom exempts a root's own path from every in-walk check
(ingest.go: 'if path == root.Path { return nil }'), so an --auto root
whose own resolved path sat under /tmp was swept whole and indexed
permanently. That is how ~495 files under /tmp/cummatrix-*/cfgpool/
reached the live manifest.

Adds NonPersistentPathPrefixes: real path prefixes (/tmp, /private/tmp,
/var/folders, /private/var/folders) checked against each auto-derived
root's own path. Applied before ExtraRoots is appended, so a repo's
declaratively-configured extra_roots keeps its documented 'swept
verbatim' contract, alongside the existing --sweep/--transcript/
--markdown bypasses.

=== 2f7f03f4 ===
refactor: green the check-full baseline — lint, decl order, gatherSources complexity
targ check-full was failing on clean main: 24 lint findings and 4 files
needing reorder-decls, all from the recently-landed pi-sessions work.
Fixed with real restructuring, no suppressions:

- gatherSources was cyclop 16/10; split into explicitSources,
  piSessionSources and sweptSources, each owning one acquisition
  mechanism, with gatherSources composing them. Its doc comment now
  records what the merge point is NOT — origin and content hash are
  both unavailable there — so a later dedup change does not assume a
  seam that isn't built yet.
- "projects" extracted to excludeDirProjects, shared by the claude and
  pi exclude lists.
- pi_sessions_test.go: JSONL fixture literals extracted to
  piSessionTranscriptContent + piRecordLine, clearing 12 lll, 6 wsl_v5
  and 2 nlreturn findings. All 8 tests and every assertion unchanged.
- update_test.go / update/update_test.go: decl order, and pi -> piHarness
  for varnamelen.

check-full now passes 7/8, the only failure being check-uncommitted.

=== 43aa09df ===
fix(prune): honour --dry-run on the default path
engram prune --dry-run reported what it would detach and then wrote the
manifest anyway: args.DryRun was read only inside pruneEmptyLocked, so
the default path's write at the end of RunPrune ran unconditionally.

The manifest write now goes through writePrunedManifest, which returns
early on a dry run, and the [dry-run] stdout prefix is shared with
pruneEmptyLocked via dryRunPrefix instead of being duplicated. Verified
with the installed binary: manifest.json is byte-identical (shasum)
across a --dry-run invocation and changes without the flag.
